Samir / team —

I parsed the workbook and sketched an initial mapping. High level recommendation (first pass):

- Steady-state: 12x A100 80GB (mixed precision FP16, KV cache enabled) — target avg throughput ~120k tokens/sec across inference fleet, typical concurrency 240 active requests.
- Burst lane: 6x H100 80GB (prefer H100 for large-context batch jobs where single-request token/sec matters) — supports short-lived 2x peak for end-of-month jobs.

Rationale and quick numbers (estimates, will refine with per-endpoint synthetic):
- A100 nodes: optimized for cost-per-token at moderate latency; expected median latency 60–80ms for gen endpoints at default batch sizing.
- H100 nodes: 30–45% higher token/sec on large seqs; better tail behavior for extreme bursts.

Suggested reservation sizing and policy:
- Commit: 12 A100 + 2 H100 baseline (guaranteed).
- Burst pool: 4 additional H100 and autoscale up to 6 for scheduled month-end windows (24h windows) with pre-warmed KV caches.

Acceptance & verification approach (summary):
1) Pre-handover synthetic replay using your workload workbook (we run same request mix against reserved pool).
2) Measure: sustained token/sec over 30m window, 99.9p tail latency, error rate.
3) Acceptance if sustained token/sec >= 95% of quoted and 99.9p latency within quoted SLO for two consecutive test runs.
4) If <95% throughput: remediation plan (hotfix scaling, model quantization toggle, temporary capacity uplift) with SLA crediting if unresolved in 72h.

Attachments referenced: helix_dedicated_workload_v2.xlsx (used for replay), will deliver a short verification playbook in next message.

Neha Kapoor

Samir / procurement —

Attached is a concise draft SOW and a delta pricing spreadsheet (high level) for the recommended configuration. Pricing highlights:

- Committed baseline (12 A100 + 2 H100): $85,000/month (covers reserved capacity, monitoring, and 8x5 support).
- Burst lane (pay-for-burst beyond baseline up to 4 H100): metered hourly at $55/hr per H100 node.
- Optional 24/7 enterprise support and priority incident handling: +$9,500/month.

Billing: monthly invoice for committed baseline, burst billed on actual consumption in the following invoice (prorated for partial months). We can provide daily usage reports for transparency.

SLA credits: defined as percentage credit of monthly committed fee when 99.9p latency and/or sustained token/sec are not met during acceptance window; formula included in the SOW (section 3.2) — typically scales with severity and duration, with an initial remediation window of 72 hours.

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Proposed next steps:

- We’ll send the finalized SOW (Rishi) and the verification playbook (Neha) by EOD tomorrow.
- Schedule a 60-minute verification planning call this Friday to confirm replay windows, test data sets, and escalation contacts (I’ll send a calendar invite once you confirm availability).

- Metric capture: sustained token/sec, 99.9p latency, error rate, KV cache hit ratio.
- If metrics meet acceptance for two consecutive runs: handover and production cutover.
- If not met: remediation steps + optional short-term capacity uplift while we fix configuration (detailed in SOW).

Confirm a good time for the call and we’ll lock it in.

Thanks,
